correctness.rationale: For fixed n>=4, maximum convex-hull area is M_n=(n/2)sin(2pi/n), uniquely at inscribed regular n-gons up to relabeling/rotation. Compactness localizes rare events and forces cyclic convex order. The ordered-angle gap density at equal gaps is (n-1)!/(2pi)^{n-1}, including labeling/rotation. Radial inward displacements u_i enter area deficit linearly with coefficient a=sin(2pi/n), and n-1 angular gaps enter with positive quadratic Gram b(I+11^T), b=a/4, determinant n b^{n-1}. Independent radial-simplex beta-ball integration gives exponent (3n-1)/2 and C_n=2^n(n-1)!/(sqrt(n)pi^{(n-1)/2}a^{(3n-1)/2}Gamma((3n+1)/2)). Remainder O(epsilon^{3/2}) on the localized mixed cap gives relative O(sqrt(epsilon)). Independently recalculated C_3=0.21780894633947 agreeing exactly with known 32/(27pi sqrt3); C_4=0.02994311458867. Finite samples and calculations do not establish all-n probability laws by themselves.

originality.rationale: Koroleva–Nikitin give regular n-gon upper endpoint laws only with vertices uniform on the circumference: their angular-only exponent is (n-1)/2; interior area-uniform sampling adds n linear radial constraints and changes the constant. Other references cover convex-position probability, lower-volume tails, or n=3; the fixed-n all-n>=4 interior law is not verified to be implied by them.
residual_risks: A historical general interior-point small-cap theorem using mixed Morse–Bott boundary coordinates might imply C_n without matching title.
No joint n->infty asymptotics, full Z_n distribution, or overlapping-subset extreme-value limit.
Monte Carlo near-tail agreement is not an analytic proof.
